enrichment.short_title: DBS mistake-of-fact appeal after oral evidence before UT
key_facts: RI, a support worker, was barred from regulated activity after MTVH concluded she stole £2,800 from a vulnerable service user; police took no further action.
The Upper Tribunal heard oral evidence from RI, found she had not stolen the money, and directed removal from the Adults' Barred List.
DBS appealed on whether the UT permissibly exercised its section 4(2)(b) mistake-of-fact jurisdiction after JHB and Kihembo.
Bean, Males and Lewis LJJ held the UT could overturn the DBS finding where credible oral evidence showed RI did not commit the impugned act.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal on points of law from the Upper Tribunal (Administrative Appeals Chamber) under section 13 TCEA 2007, following parallel guidance in DBS v JHB and Kihembo v DBS.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal dismissed; UT decision removing RI from the Adults' Barred List upheld.
enrichment.ratio: On a section 4(2)(b) SGVA appeal the UT may hear oral evidence and, if satisfied on the balance of probabilities that the barred person did not do the relevant act, find a mistake of fact; that is not reducible to Wednesbury review of paper findings or to requiring wholly new documentary evidence, and JHB is confined to cases where the UT hears no relevant oral evidence.
legal_issues: Scope of UT mistake-of-fact jurisdiction under section 4(2)(b) SGVA 2006
Interaction of PF v DBS, JHB and Kihembo authorities
Whether oral credibility findings by the UT constitute impermissible re-evaluation of DBS paper decision

enrichment.short_title: Atos Section Rule 21 shortfall and Article 7 Protection Order

statutes_considered.title: Railway Pensions (Protection and Designation of Schemes) Order 1994 (SI 1994/1432)

key_facts: The Atos Section of the Railways Pension Scheme had a large deficit with very few active members funding past-service liabilities.
Atos argued Rule 21 required full shortfall repair by actuarial calculation; the trustee said the actuary exercises professional judgment and Article 7 imposes a freestanding employer top-up.
The Chancellor held Rule 21 was not an exhaustive code and Article 7 imposed a balance-of-cost obligation after Rule 21(1)(ii).
The Court of Appeal upheld that construction and dismissed Atos's appeal.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal from the Chancellor's construction judgment in Part 8 proceedings on the Atos Section Rules and the Protection Order.
enrichment.ratio: Rule 21(1) shortfall repair is not a mandatory full elimination code; 'determine' in Rule 21(1)(ii) and (iv) imports actuarial professional judgment including collectability; Article 7(1) of the Protection Order imposes a freestanding sufficiency-of-funding obligation on employers of Protected Persons, taking effect after Rule 21(1)(ii).
legal_issues: Whether Rule 21 is an exhaustive shortfall elimination regime
Meaning of 'as determined by the Actuary' in Rule 21(1)(ii) and (iv)
Relationship between Rule 21 and Article 7 Protection Order funding duties

In re Courage Group's Pension Schemes

key_facts: Following a successful financial remedy appeal, the wife sought £425,000 costs including return of £175,000 LSPO and £250,000 appeal costs.

enrichment.short_title: CPR Part 71 committal appeal and jurisdiction
key_facts: Judgment creditor Roberts pursued Part 71 information orders against debtor Jones over a caravan rent debt; Jones repeatedly failed to attend.
On 5 April 2022 Jones was arrested and questioned by a court officer without creditor notice; HHJ Beard imposed 14 days suspended imprisonment.
The Court of Appeal held the creditor's appeal route was to the High Court not direct to the CA under section 13; Birss LJ sat as HC judge to decide merits.
Suspended sentence quashed for defective November 2021 order; slip-rule amendment struck out; matter remitted for questioning before judge with creditor notice.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal (reconstituted as High Court appeal under Massie v H and M) against Part 71 suspended committal and procedural orders.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed in part: suspended sentence quashed, slip-rule amendment set aside, Part 71 proceedings remitted to county court.
enrichment.ratio: A judgment creditor's appeal from a Part 71 committal is to the High Court not the Court of Appeal under section 13 AJA 1960; questioning under an order requiring examination before a judge cannot proceed before a court officer without notice to the creditor; a defective suspended committal order without specified sentence cannot support later activation.
legal_issues: Route of appeal from Part 71 committal orders
Proper conduct of judgment debtor examination under CPR Part 71
Validity of suspended committal where no sentence specified
Permissible use of CPR 40.12 slip rule

enrichment.short_title: SPC product definition for safinamide Parkinson's therapy
key_facts: Newron sought an SPC for safinamide (Xadago) based on EP (UK) 1 613 296 claiming safinamide with levodopa/PDI for Parkinson's disease.

enrichment.short_title: Ex turpi defence unavailable after NGRI insanity verdict
key_facts: Lewis-Ranwell killed three men during psychotic episode; found not guilty by reason of insanity and detained under sections 37/41 MHA 1983.
He sued police, NHS trust, G4S and council for negligent release before killings; defendants sought strike-out on ex turpi causa.
Garnham J held NGRI verdict meant no requisite turpitude; illegality defence unavailable.
Majority (Underhill LJ and Sharp P) dismissed appeal; Andrews LJ dissenting would allow and strike out negligence claim.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal against refusal to strike out negligence claim on ex turpi/illegality grounds (Human Rights Act claim unaffected).
enrichment.outcome: Appeal dismissed by majority; negligence claim may proceed alongside HRA claim.
enrichment.ratio: A verdict of not guilty by reason of insanity under the M'Naghten rules means the defendant did not know his acts were wrong and lacks the turpitude required for ex turpi causa; illegality defence therefore unavailable as a matter of law for the negligence claim arising from pre-offence failures, though Andrews LJ dissenting would align NGRI with Clunis/Gray/Henderson.
legal_issues: Whether ex turpi applies where claimant acquitted NGRI for homicide
Distinction between insanity and diminished responsibility for illegality defence
Application of Patel v Mirza policy approach to mental illness

storyline.title: NGRI killer's negligence claim survives ex turpi challenge
storyline.summary: After being found not guilty by reason of insanity for three killings, Lewis-Ranwell sued those who had released him from custody. The Court of Appeal majority held ex turpi could not bar the claim because insanity negated turpitude.

parties.name: G4S Health Services (UK) Ltd and others

stages.title: Two pre-offence arrests
stages.what_happened: Claimant arrested twice; mental health assessment not completed; released.

stages.title: Three homicides committed
stages.what_happened: Claimant killed three elderly men during psychotic episode in Exeter.

stages.title: NGRI verdict at trial
stages.what_happened: Jury found not guilty by reason of insanity; hospital order with restrictions.

stages.title: High Court claim issued
stages.what_happened: Negligence and HRA section 7 claims against police, trust, G4S and council.

stages.title: Strike-out applications issued
stages.what_happened: G4S, trust and council applied to strike negligence claim on ex turpi grounds.

stages.title: Garnham J dismisses applications
stages.what_happened: Held NGRI verdict meant no knowing wrongfulness; no turpitude for ex turpi.

stages.title: Insanity distinguished from diminished responsibility
stages.what_happened: Gray and Henderson on diminished responsibility not determinative; foreign cases favour no ex turpi for insanity.

stages.title: Andrews LJ dissent
stages.what_happened: Would allow appeal; deliberate killing should not support negligence claim despite lack of knowledge of wrong.

stages.title: Appeal dismissed
stages.what_happened: Underhill LJ and Sharp P dismissed appeal; negligence claim proceeds.
stages.why_it_matters: Claimants with NGRI verdict may sue for pre-offence negligence.

turning_points.label: Insanity not turpitude
turning_points.impact: Majority's basis for rejecting ex turpi.
